PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: State assertion
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A subject has or enters a named state.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: State transition
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A subject transitions between states because of a trigger.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Behavior guard
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A condition gates or forbids behavior for a subject.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Exception rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A required behavior is skipped when a named exception condition holds.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Mutual exclusion
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: Two modes, states, options, or behaviors cannot be true or active together.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Dependency rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A subject requires a prerequisite before a dependent action or state can proceed.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Ownership rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A resource or behavior is owned by a service, team, role, or component.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Retry policy
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A failed subject or action retries up to a bounded attempt count.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Escalation rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A failed or unresolved subject escalates to an owner after a bounded delay.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Availability SLA
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A service or API must meet a minimum availability target over a reporting window.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Notification route
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A subject notifies a target recipient through a specific channel.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Idempotency rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A request or operation must deduplicate repeated execution by a stable idempotency key.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Data residency rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: A data set must be stored, processed, or kept within a named region or jurisdiction.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Audit event rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: An action, change, or security-relevant event must be recorded in an audit log or audit trail.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Consent rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: An action or processing purpose requires a named consent before it proceeds.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.title: Lifecycle rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_1.description: An entity must be archived, deleted, expired, or lifecycle-transitioned after a duration.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Conflict resolution rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Concurrent or synchronized updates resolve conflicts with a named strategy.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Fallback rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A degraded or unavailable dependency causes a subject to fall back to an alternative behavior.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Batch operation rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A bulk operation processes a resource in batches of a bounded size.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Consistency rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: An entity reference or value must remain consistent with another existing entity or invariant.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Build constraint
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Build-time generation or deployment configuration must satisfy a deterministic property.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Environment safety rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A named action is allowed or forbidden in a deployment environment.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Schema invariant rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A schema field has an invariant such as immutability, type, enum, or value range.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Coding standard rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Developer-facing code must use or avoid a framework API, pattern, or documentation practice.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Migration boundary rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Legacy data or APIs may only be used for migration or compatibility input.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Absence requirement
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A component, extension, RPC, schema, or feature must be absent, removed, or not exist.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Offline behavior rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Synchronization or gameplay behavior remains non-blocking or resilient during offline conditions.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Release gate rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A build or release must pass named gates before distribution, review, or deployment.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Platform consistency rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A state or entitlement synchronizes across named platforms.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Preservation rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Child data or feedback is preserved across deletion or removal of a parent resource.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Abstraction boundary rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: Persisted data, APIs, or contracts must stay neutral to a renderer, vendor, runtime, or implementation detail.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.title: Security configuration rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_2.description: A security-sensitive component must have an explicit configuration value.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Ordered strategy rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject must use strategies in a required priority order.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Refresh policy rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject refreshes a target automatically or by a named policy.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Scoped authorization rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A scoped actor is allowed or denied an action because of assignment, ownership, or membership.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Documentation standard rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject must be documented in a named documentation artifact.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Warmup policy rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject must warm up on a named trigger or entry point.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Visual layout rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A UI subject must remain visually aligned or layout-consistent with a target.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Enforcement location rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A constraint or policy must be enforced at a named system layer.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Reconciliation rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A trigger reconciles a target and performs a stale-data cleanup action.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Throttle policy rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: Handlers or operations must be throttled for a named activity class.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Unsaved change state
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject has unsaved or dirty local edits.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Commit or save action
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A trigger commits, saves, or persists a subject within a scope.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Discard action
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A trigger discards or cancels changes for a subject within a scope.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Accessibility requirement
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject must satisfy an accessibility standard or severity target.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Retention policy
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject is retained for a bounded duration.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.title: Resource constraint
PREDICATE_CATALOG_3.description: A subject constrains a resource by operator, threshold, and unit.
paraphrase_templates: must complete in under a bounded duration
must stay at a bounded frame rate
must respond within a time budget

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Dependency resolution policy
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: Defines where a component may resolve a dependency and how it may acquire it.
argument_descriptions: Component performing resolution.
Dependency to resolve.
Permitted resolution scope.
Allowed acquisition behavior.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Ordered resolution strategy
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: Defines ordered sources for resolving a dependency and the condition for fallback.
argument_descriptions: Resolver applying the strategy.
Sources tried in order.
Condition permitting fallback.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Resolution failure policy
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: Defines the required outcome when dependency resolution encounters invalid or ambiguous inputs.
argument_descriptions: Resolver enforcing the policy.
Invalid or ambiguous condition.
Required failure outcome.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Process delegation contract
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: Defines executable, working-directory, environment, stdio, and termination behavior for a delegated child process.
argument_descriptions: Launcher delegating the process.
Executable selection policy.
Working-directory policy.
Environment policy.
Standard I/O policy.
Termination and exit propagation policy.
examples: process_delegation_contract(launcher, resolved_executable, consumer_cwd, inherited_env, piped_stdio, propagate_exit)

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Failure behavior
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: Defines the required outcome when a component encounters a named failure condition.
argument_descriptions: Component experiencing failure.
Failure condition.
Required observable outcome.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Feature gate
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject is controlled by a runtime or configuration gate.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Event publication
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject publishes a domain or system event.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Acceptance rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject has an observable acceptance outcome.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Permission rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: An actor is allowed or denied an action against a resource.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Default value
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject property defaults to a value.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Uniqueness constraint
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject is unique within one or more scope keys.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: State membership
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A state-valued subject has a closed set of allowed states.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Temporal order
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: One event or state must occur before or after another.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Conditional behavior
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A behavior follows when a condition is true.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: State transition
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: A subject moves from one state to another because of a trigger.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.title: Rate limit
PREDICATE_CATALOG_4.description: An action is limited to a count within a time window.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Fail-closed authorization rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: On invalid, missing, or failed authorization input the subject must deny access or stay unauthenticated instead of falling back to a default identity.
argument_descriptions: Component or route that must fail closed.
Invalid, missing, or failed authorization condition.
Required denied outcome, such as staying unauthenticated or redirecting to login.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Deployment precondition rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: A deployment or rollout must hold or abort until a named precondition holds, such as no unsupported legacy data remaining.
argument_descriptions: System, service, or release being deployed.
Precondition that must hold before deployment proceeds.
Required action when the precondition fails, such as holding deployment.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Data migration rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: Legacy data converts to the canonical form in a bounded, verified sequence, typically once and without data loss, before canonical-only operation begins.
argument_descriptions: Legacy payload, table, or format being converted.
Canonical payload, table, or format produced by the conversion.
Sequencing contract, such as one-time conversion or conversion before canonical-only reads.
aliases: converted once with no data loss

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Diagnostic visibility rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: Internal error and transport detail stays confined to logs or debugging surfaces while user-facing surfaces show actionable, friendly messages.
argument_descriptions: Flow or component whose diagnostics are governed.
Internal detail such as raw payloads, status lines, or backend errors.
User-facing surface and its required message style.
Log or debugging surface where internal detail is confined.
aliases: logged and must not be shown

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Mutation authority rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: A client-facing surface exposes only its declared mutation scope; authority for other mutations stays server-side.
argument_descriptions: Client, view, API, or table surface being constrained.
Declared mutation scope, such as read-only or no direct writes.
Server-side authority, such as database triggers or an RPC, that owns other mutations.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Request deduplication rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: Concurrent duplicate requests for the same resource are coalesced into one underlying operation, preventing redundant work.
argument_descriptions: Component issuing the requests.
Request or query being deduplicated.
Scope of deduplication, such as the same user or key.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Async boundary rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: A callback or handler must return synchronously, without awaiting, while work runs deferred or in the background.
argument_descriptions: Callback, handler, or API boundary.
Operation that must not block the caller.
Required policy, such as return synchronously or defer to background.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Canonical identifier rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: References to a domain entity must resolve through one canonical identifier or key.
argument_descriptions: Domain entity or flow being referenced.
The canonical identifier or key.
Required resolution behavior for routes, lookups, or messaging.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Responsive breakpoint rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: A viewport is classified by explicit responsive breakpoints, such as landscape phones counting as mobile below a height threshold.
argument_descriptions: UI or layout being classified.
Viewport condition with explicit dimensions.
Resulting classification, such as mobile or desktop.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.title: Operational pause rule
PREDICATE_CATALOG_5.description: An operational pause or kill switch blocks new operations of a kind while preserving already-started or completed work.
argument_descriptions: Operational control being paused.
New operations the pause must block.
Existing work the pause must preserve, such as resumable sessions.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.title: UI pattern
PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.description: A UI concept must be presented with a named visual pattern, such as a line-and-dots timeline or a card list.
argument_descriptions: The UI concept or region, such as an annotation list.
The agreed visual pattern for that concept.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.title: Same pattern across variants
PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.description: Two variants of a UI concept (roles, viewports, presentations) must use the same visual pattern.
argument_descriptions: The UI concept whose variants must not diverge.
One variant, such as a role or presentation.
The variant that must match it.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.title: Pattern marker
PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.description: A visual pattern is recognisable in code by a stable marker such as a CSS class or test id.
argument_descriptions: The visual pattern the marker belongs to.
Literal class name or test id that implementations of the pattern contain.

PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.title: UI container
PREDICATE_CATALOG_6.description: A UI region must sit in a container of a given size with a given overflow behaviour.
argument_descriptions: The UI region the container holds.
Container size, such as half_page or full_height.
Overflow behaviour, such as scroll or clip.

use_when: Use for one subject being in, entering, or requiring one named state.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for allowed state sets or explicit state-to-state movement; use state_membership or state_transition instead.

use_when: Use for workflow prose where a subject moves between states because of a trigger.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for one current state, allowed terminal states, or non-state conditional behavior.

use_when: Use when a boolean condition gates whether behavior is active or permitted.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for explicit unless/except exceptions, actor authorization, feature flags, or scalar thresholds.

use_when: Use for unless/except clauses where a normally required behavior is skipped under a named exception.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic boolean guards without an exception clause, actor permissions, or feature flags.

use_when: Use when two modes, states, options, or behaviors cannot be true or active together.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for uniqueness per scope, allowed state sets, or ordinary permission denials.

use_when: Use when one action, state, or resource requires another prerequisite before it can proceed.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for temporal ordering without a required prerequisite, ownership, or feature gates.

use_when: Use when a resource, domain area, or behavior is owned by a service, team, role, or component.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for permission to access a resource or event publication.

use_when: Use when a failed action must be retried a bounded number of times or attempts.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for rate limits, backoff timing without retries, or escalation after a delay.

use_when: Use when an unresolved or failed condition is escalated to an owner, role, queue, or service after a delay.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ownership assignments, retry counts, or simple notification routing.

use_when: Use when an API, service, or system has a minimum availability target over a reporting window.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for latency thresholds, retention durations, or generic resource constraints.

use_when: Use when a subject must notify a recipient, team, or role through a specific channel.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for event publication, ownership assignment, or escalation after a delay.

use_when: Use when repeated, redundant, or concurrent requests or operations must be safely deduplicated by an idempotency key or equivalent identity.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for general uniqueness constraints, retry counts, or rate limits; choose the more specific predicate instead.

use_when: Use when data must be stored, processed, or kept within a named region or jurisdiction.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for retention durations, access permissions, or notification routing.

use_when: Use when an action, change, or security-relevant event must be recorded in an audit log or audit trail.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for user-facing notifications, event publication, or generic dirty-change state.

use_when: Use when an action or data-processing purpose requires explicit user consent before it proceeds.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for data residency, permission denials, or retention durations.

use_when: Use when an entity must be archived, deleted, expired, or otherwise lifecycle-transitioned after a duration.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for passive retention duration requirements; use retention_policy when data is simply kept for a period.

use_when: Use when synchronization or concurrent updates require a named conflict-resolution strategy.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary state transitions, dependency ordering, or fallback behavior.

use_when: Use when a degraded or unavailable dependency causes a subject to fall back to a named alternative behavior.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for escalation after a delay, notification routing, or retry policies.

use_when: Use when a bulk operation must process a resource in batches of a specific size.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for rate limits, retry counts, or general resource thresholds.

use_when: Use when one entity must reference, match, or remain consistent with another existing entity or invariant.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ownership, permission checks, or prerequisite workflow dependencies.

use_when: Use when build-time generation or deployment configuration must satisfy a deterministic property.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for runtime feature gates or ordinary resource thresholds.

use_when: Use when an action is allowed or forbidden in a named environment such as production or staging.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for actor permissions that are independent of deployment environment.

use_when: Use when a schema field has an invariant such as immutability, type, enum, or value-range constraints.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for cross-entity references; use consistency_rule for referential integrity.

use_when: Use when developer-facing code must use or avoid a framework API, pattern, or documentation practice.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for user-facing product behavior or role-based access control.

use_when: Use when legacy data or APIs may only be used for migration or compatibility input.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for general lifecycle archive/delete timing rules.

use_when: Use when a component, extension, RPC, schema, or feature must be absent, removed, or not exist.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for denied user actions; use permission_rule for actor/action/resource denials.

use_when: Use when synchronization or gameplay behavior must remain non-blocking or resilient during offline conditions.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic fallback behavior without an offline/resilient synchronization condition.

use_when: Use when builds or releases must pass named gates before distribution, review, or deployment.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for runtime dependency prerequisites; use dependency_rule for product workflow dependencies.

use_when: Use when a state or entitlement must synchronize across named platforms.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for referential integrity within one data model; use consistency_rule instead.

use_when: Use when child data or feedback must be preserved across deletion/removal of a parent resource.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for simple archive/delete timing rules without a preservation target.

use_when: Use when persisted data, APIs, or contracts must remain neutral to a renderer, vendor, runtime, or implementation detail.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic coding standards without a boundary/contract target; use coding_standard_rule instead.

use_when: Use when infrastructure, database, trigger, RPC, or deployment components must carry an explicit security configuration value.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for actor authorization decisions; use permission_rule or scoped_authorization_rule instead.

use_when: Use when a subject must apply named strategies in a required priority or fallback order.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for unordered enum membership; use strict allowed_values or state_membership instead.

use_when: Use when a UI, dashboard, cache, or list must refresh a target automatically or on a named cadence/trigger.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for save/commit actions or notification routing; use commit_action or notification_route instead.

use_when: Use when an actor is allowed or denied an action because they are assigned, unassigned, owner, member, or otherwise scoped to a resource.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for simple actor/action/resource permissions without a scope qualifier; use permission_rule instead.

use_when: Use when code symbols, APIs, tests, or project artifacts must be documented in a named documentation source.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for runtime persistence or user-facing display labels.

use_when: Use when a component, media element, cache, or service must warm up on a named entry or trigger.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic state transitions without warmup behavior.

use_when: Use when UI elements must remain visually aligned, consistent, or layout-compatible with another element.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic acceptance outcomes without a visual/layout relationship.

use_when: Use when a constraint or policy must be enforced at a named layer such as database, application, edge, or client level.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for the constraint itself when the enforcement location is not stated.

use_when: Use when a trigger requires reconciling a target and clearing stale or inconsistent records.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary archive/delete timing without reconciliation.

use_when: Use when handlers, operations, or streams must be throttled for high-frequency activity.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for numeric API request quotas; use rate_limit instead.

use_when: Use for dirty, draft, or unsaved local-edit state on a subject.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for the action that saves or discards those changes.

use_when: Use when a trigger saves, commits, persists, or auto-saves a subject in a scope.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for cancel, discard, revert, or abandon behavior.

use_when: Use when a trigger discards, cancels, reverts, or abandons changes in a scope.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for persistence or save behavior.

use_when: Use for WCAG, keyboard, screen-reader, or accessibility target requirements.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic acceptance outcomes or performance constraints.

use_when: Use when records or data must be retained for a bounded duration.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for request rate windows, session expiry, or latency thresholds.

use_when: Use for resource, latency, timeout, size, quota, or numeric threshold constraints.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for uniqueness, rate limits, feature gates, or actor permissions.

use_when: Use when behavior is controlled by a runtime/config flag, kill switch, or feature gate.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for actor authorization or ordinary scalar enabled/disabled properties.

use_when: Use when a subject publishes, emits, or raises a domain/system event.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for consuming events or observable UI acceptance outcomes.

use_when: Use for observable acceptance outcomes such as visible empty states or displayed results.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for internal state machines, event publication, or accessibility standards.

use_when: Use for allow/deny permission statements with an actor, action, and resource.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for scalar quotas, feature flags, or state transitions; choose a more specific predicate or strict property instead.

use_when: Use when behavior defines a default mode, state, status, option, or value.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for current-state assertions or allowed value sets.

use_when: Use when a component's permitted dependency scope and acquisition/download policy are normative.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordering among multiple candidates, invalid-input outcomes, or child-process execution details.

use_when: Use when resolution must try named sources in a defined order with a conditional fallback.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for a general dependency scope policy, invalid resolution errors, or process launch behavior.

use_when: Use when invalid placeholders, ambiguous roots, or other resolution inputs require a specific rejection outcome.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary missing-dependency reporting or successful lookup ordering.

use_when: Use when a launcher delegates to a child process and specifies executable, cwd, environment, stdio, or termination behavior.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for dependency lookup, package-manager exceptions, or generic failure reporting.

use_when: Use when a component must define the observable outcome of a named failure such as a missing dependency.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for resolution ordering, invalid-input policy details, or exception clauses that exempt a normal rule.

use_when: Use for at-most-one or unique-per-scope constraints.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for numeric caps where more than one instance may be valid.

use_when: Use for terminal, allowed, or enumerated state sets.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for one current state or a transition between states.

use_when: Use for before/after ordering requirements between events, states, or actions.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when source state, target state, and trigger are all explicit; use state_transition instead.

use_when: Use for if/when conditional prose where a condition leads to a behavior.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for simple boolean guards or actor permission rules.

use_when: Use for explicit transitions from one named state to another with a trigger.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for a single state assertion or an allowed terminal-state set.

use_when: Use for per-window request, attempt, or action limits.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for resource thresholds that lack a repeated action and time window.

use_when: Use when invalid, missing, or failed authorization input must deny access or stay unauthenticated.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when a degraded dependency legitimately falls back to a named alternative behavior.

use_when: Use when a deployment or rollout must hold or abort until a named precondition holds.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for feature flags, checkout flows, or ordinary release test gates.

use_when: Use when legacy data converts to a canonical form once, without data loss, before canonical-only operation.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for a standing boundary that only permits legacy reads as migration input.

use_when: Use when internal error or transport detail must stay in logs while users see actionable messages.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for audit-trail requirements or consent handling.

use_when: Use when a client surface is read-only or scoped and a server-side authority owns the other mutations.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for individual permission denials such as delete or export rights.

use_when: Use when concurrent duplicate requests for the same resource must coalesce into one operation.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for per-window rate limits or batch-size constraints.

use_when: Use when a callback must return synchronously while work runs deferred or in the background.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for timeout durations or request rate constraints.

use_when: Use when references to a domain entity must resolve through one canonical identifier or key.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for renderer neutrality or legacy-format boundaries.

use_when: Use when explicit viewport dimensions determine a responsive classification such as mobile.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for server-side size limits or database constraints.

use_when: Use when an operational pause blocks new work of a kind while preserving existing or resumable work.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for soft deletion or data preservation rules without an operational switch.

use_when: Use when a UI concept must be presented with a named visual pattern that other screens or variants must not replace.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for alignment between two elements (visual_layout_rule) or for colours and spacing a linter can check.

use_when: Use when two variants of one UI concept, such as roles or presentations, must render the same visual pattern.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the variants are intentionally different; record that difference in the requirement instead.

use_when: Use to name a stable class or test id that every implementation of a visual pattern contains.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for markers that change with content or styling, such as generated class names.

use_when: Use when a UI region must sit in a container of a named size with a named overflow behaviour, such as a half-page scroll panel.
do_not_use_when: Do not use for exact pixel sizes or brand tokens a linter or stylesheet already enforces.

use_when: Use when the prose matches this predicate signature and all required arguments can be named explicitly.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when a stricter scalar property, a more specific predicate, or an ontology-gap observation better preserves the claim.
